title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 101-102
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 101 to 102 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'अनादिर्भूर्भुवो लक्ष्मीः सुवीरो रुचिराङ्गदः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 101 to 102 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 101 to 102.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 101 to 102** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **अनादिर्भूर्भुवो लक्ष्मीः सुवीरो रुचिराङ्गदः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**अनादिर्भूर्भुवो लक्ष्मीः सुवीरो रुचिराङ्गदः । जननो जनजन्मादिर्भीमो भीमपराक्रमः ॥** **आधारनिलयोऽधाता पुष्पहासः प्रजागरः । ऊर्ध्वगः सत्पथाचारः प्राणदः प्रणवः पणः ॥**

He has no beginning, he is earth, sky and Lakshmi herself. The brave one with lovely armlets is that God of gods. He gives birth, the origin of all people, fearsome and of terrible might. The support of all and himself unsupported, with a blooming smile, ever awake is he. The one who lifts us higher and walks the path of the good is that God of gods. He gives life, he is Om, and he is the praise.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 101 to 102 mean?
faq.a: He has no beginning, he is earth, sky and Lakshmi herself. The brave one with lovely armlets is that God of gods. He gives birth, the origin of all people, fearsome and of terrible might. The support of all and himself unsupported, with a blooming smile, ever awake is he. The one who lifts us higher and walks the path of the good is that God of gods. He gives life, he is Om, and he is the praise.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
